scope.flow: ERC-4337 UserOp validation for unclaimed AtomWallet via validateUserOp/owner() reading MultiVault storage
scope.environment: ERC-4337 bundlers (Pimlico, Alchemy, Infinitism, compliant bundlers) simulating UserOps against AtomWallet and MultiVault

statements.text: The AtomWallet is in the unclaimed state (isClaimed is false).
MultiVault is not staked in the EntryPoint; it is a plain protocol contract.
A UserOp for the unclaimed AtomWallet is submitted to a compliant bundler for simulation.
validateUserOp execution calls _validateSignature, which calls owner() at L309.
For an unclaimed AtomWallet, owner() reads storage from MultiVault via the getAtomWarden() external call during validateUserOp.
During validateUserOp, an account may only access its own storage, or the storage of entities staked in the EntryPoint (paymasters, factories).
validateUserOp must not SLOAD from the storage of a contract that is not staked in the EntryPoint.
After a wallet is claimed (isClaimed = true), owner() reads from the wallet's own local storage slot rather than MultiVault.
The entire protocol's ERC-4337 infrastructure is non-functional by default because every AtomWallet is deployed in the unclaimed state.
The atomWarden cannot use UserOps to interact with unclaimed wallets through bundlers.
Sponsored transactions, paymasters, and any bundler-based gas abstraction are unavailable until a wallet is individually claimed.
Claiming a wallet requires a direct on-chain transaction, defeating the purpose of the AA design.

ambiguities: Report does not state whether a specific UserOp was actually submitted; the trigger is conditional on a compliant bundler simulating one.
No explicit statement that anyone can call validateUserOp; caller authorization is not specified.
The exact storage slot read from MultiVault is not identified beyond the getAtomWarden() external call.
The report notes the violation disappears post-claim because isClaimed = true causes owner() to read from the wallet's own local storage slot instead.
